children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by understanding your situation. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about the child(ren) you're claiming for.

**First, what is the age of the child you're claiming for?**

- **Under 16 years old**
- **16-19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Please let me know which category applies to your child, and if you're claiming for multiple children, I'll need to check each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 21 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context. Let me navigate through the assessment with the information you've given me.

Since Alex is 21 years old (20 or over), let me check the eligibility outcome for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

**Reason:**
Child Benefit can only be paid for a child who is:
- Under 16 years old, OR
- Aged 16-19 and in approved education or training (such as secondary school, college, or certain training schemes)

Since Alex is 21 years old, they no longer fall into either qualifying category. Child Benefit typically stops when a child reaches 16, unless they continue in approved full-time education or training, in which case it can continue until they turn 20 (with specific conditions).

**Important to note:**
- If Alex had just turned 20 and was still in approved education or training at that point, the benefit would have stopped
- If Alex left education at 16 or 17, there would have been a 20-week grace period if registered with the careers service or armed services

If you have any other children who are under 16 or aged 16-19 in approved education/training, I'd be happy to check their eligibility. Otherwise, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit at this time.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this, or do you have other children you'd like me to check?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. No, Alex is my only child, so I suppose that's that then.

Thank you for checking and explaining it to me. At least I know where I stand now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify your situation. It's disappointing news, but at least you now have a clear understanding of why you're not eligible and where the rules stand.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you become a guardian for a younger child or have other dependents—feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility.

Thank you for using this service, and I wish you all the best!
